definitions.explanation: Machines, tools, and materials needed for a specific task or activity. Commonly used for film/video equipment, audio gear, construction materials, and other specialized equipment that is transported and set up for use.

examples.japanese: {撮影|さつえい}{機材|きざい}を{準備|じゅんび}する。
{重|おも}い{機材|きざい}を{運|はこ}ぶのは{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: It's tough to carry heavy equipment.

examples.japanese: コンサートの{前|まえ}に、スタッフが{音響|おんきょう}{機材|きざい}のセッティングを{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: Before the concert, the staff set up the audio equipment.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{機|き} (machine, mechanism) + {材|ざい} (material, timber). Literally "machine materials" — the machines and materials needed for work.

USAGE:
{機材|きざい} implies portable or deployable equipment — things you bring to a location, set up, and use. It is commonly associated with film/video production, audio engineering, photography, construction, and events. Unlike {機器|きき} (which emphasizes the devices themselves), {機材|きざい} includes the idea of materials and supplies alongside the machines.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {撮影|さつえい}{機材|きざい}: filming/photography equipment
- {音響|おんきょう}{機材|きざい}: audio equipment
- {照明|しょうめい}{機材|きざい}: lighting equipment
- {機材|きざい}を{搬入|はんにゅう}する: to bring in equipment
- {機材|きざい}トラブル: equipment trouble

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {機器|きき}: equipment, devices (more formal, technical)
- {器具|きぐ}: instruments, utensils (smaller items)
- {道具|どうぐ}: tools (general, everyday)
